introBody: Nine periods, sixteen releases, and eighteen concert photographs with named creators. The earliest release is the Kill Kill EP (2008); the newest entry is Stove, still unreleased on 24 November 2026.
Dates and chart positions point to the references on the Sources page. Photographs are stored locally with the creator, file page, and licence attached.

eras.label: Lizzy Grant
eras.title: Lizzy Grant & the early recordings
eras.summary: Church choirs, school bands, Brooklyn clubs, and two records made as Lizzy Grant.
eras.lede: Elizabeth Woolridge Grant was born in New York City on 21 June 1985 and grew up in Lake Placid. Music came first through church and school, then through small clubs in Brooklyn and New Jersey, where she performed under names including Sparkle Jump Rope Queen and Lizzy Grant.

sections.heading: The first releases
body: After studying philosophy at Fordham University, Grant worked with producer David Kahne. The three-song Kill Kill EP appeared in October 2008 on 5 Points Records; the album Lana Del Ray followed in January 2010.
Both records were issued under her own name. They open the chronology, before the stage name and the major-label debut.

sections.heading: The name change
body: The Lizzy Grant records went out of print. Later releases used the name Lana Del Rey, with wider production and the 2011 video for “Video Games”.
This chapter stays separate from Born to Die because the two records were made under a different name and released on a different label.

facts.label: Early aliases
facts.value: Sparkle Jump Rope Queen; Lizzy Grant; May Jailer

eras.label: Born to Die / Paradise
eras.title: Born to Die, Paradise, and the bright dark
eras.summary: The 2011 “Video Games” video, the January 2012 major-label debut, and the Paradise EP that followed.
eras.lede: The “Video Games” video arrived in 2011 with a homemade Super 8 quality and a chorus that felt older than the internet. By the time Born to Die was released in January 2012, the song had already changed the scale of the project.

sections.heading: A major-label debut
body: Born to Die arrived on 27 January 2012 through Stranger, Interscope, and Polydor. Its 12-track standard edition mixed baroque pop, trip hop, and strings; the deluxe edition added “Without You”, “Lolita”, and “Lucky Ones”. The album peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and topped charts in Australia, France, Germany, and the UK.
In December 2025, Billboard reported 618 weeks on the Billboard 200 for Born to Die, the longest run by an album from a female artist in the chart’s history.

sections.heading: Paradise and the film
body: Paradise followed in November 2012: eight tracks, including “Ride”, “American”, “Cola”, and “Gods & Monsters”, plus the iTunes bonus “Burning Desire”. The following year, the 27-minute short film Tropico threaded “Body Electric”, “Gods & Monsters”, and “Bel Air” into a three-chapter narrative.

The videos and cover art used Americana imagery: motels, wide skies, and long takes. “Young and Beautiful” and the Cedric Gervais remix of “Summertime Sadness” carried the era into film and radio in 2013.

facts.value: Video Games; Born to Die; Blue Jeans; Ride; Young and Beautiful

eras.label: Ultraviolence
eras.title: Ultraviolence and the guitar
eras.summary: Released 13 June 2014 with Dan Auerbach as a central collaborator and live guitars across the record.
eras.lede: Ultraviolence was released on 13 June 2014. After the orchestral scale of Born to Die and Paradise, the third album moved toward live guitar, desert-rock space, and a rawer vocal presence, with Dan Auerbach of the Black Keys as a central collaborator.

sections.heading: The record
body: The 11-track standard edition opens with “Cruel World” and includes “West Coast”, “Brooklyn Baby”, “Money Power Glory”, and “The Other Woman”. Dan Auerbach produced much of the album with Del Rey.

It debuted at No. 1 in eleven countries, including the United States, and reached the top five in more than twenty territories. The deluxe edition added “Black Beauty”, “Guns and Roses”, and “Florida Kilos”.

sections.heading: Outside the album
body: The era also produced “Big Eyes” and “I Can Fly” for Tim Burton’s film Big Eyes (2014).
The photographs in this chapter come from Coachella and Rock en Seine in 2014.

eras.label: Honeymoon
eras.title: Honeymoon in slow motion
eras.summary: Fourteen tracks released 18 September 2015, produced by Del Rey with Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies.
eras.lede: Honeymoon arrived on 18 September 2015: fourteen tracks, 65 minutes, and a deliberate step back toward the baroque pop of Born to Die after the guitar-heavy Ultraviolence. It was produced by Del Rey with Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies.

sections.heading: The record
body: The album opens with the title track and moves through “Music to Watch Boys To”, “Terrence Loves You”, “High by the Beach”, “Freak”, and “The Blackest Day”. “Burnt Norton” sets a passage of T. S. Eliot over an interlude; “Don’t Let Me Be Misunderstood” closes the record.
It peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and reached the top five in more than twenty countries. Del Rey produced it with Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies.

sections.heading: The tour
body: The Endless Summer Tour took the album across North America in 2015, with Courtney Love and Grimes on selected dates. In 2016, Del Rey appeared on the Weeknd’s “Starboy”.
The Honeymoon photographs come from Sasquatch! in 2015. They show Del Rey at a distance under stage lights.

eras.label: Lust for Life
eras.title: Lust for Life and the open door
eras.summary: Released 21 July 2017 with guest appearances from Stevie Nicks, the Weeknd, A$AP Rocky, and Sean Ono Lennon.
eras.lede: Lust for Life was released on 21 July 2017. It is the first Del Rey album that sounds like a group conversation: the Weeknd, A$AP Rocky, Playboi Carti, Stevie Nicks, and Sean Ono Lennon all pass through it.

sections.heading: A wider cast
body: The 16-track album includes “Love”, “Lust for Life”, “13 Beaches”, “Cherry”, “Summer Bummer”, “Groupie Love”, and “Get Free”. It topped the charts in twelve countries, including the US and the UK, and was nominated for Best Pop Vocal Album at the 60th Grammy Awards.
The credits list the Weeknd, A$AP Rocky, Playboi Carti, Stevie Nicks, and Sean Ono Lennon among the guest artists.

sections.heading: The visual turn
body: The “Love” video was directed by Rich Lee. The cover shows Del Rey in front of a truck.
The 2017 festival photographs in this chapter are from Flow Festival in Helsinki and KROQ Weenie Roast in California.

eras.label: Norman Fucking Rockwell!
eras.title: Norman Fucking Rockwell! and the long exhale
eras.summary: Released 30 August 2019 with Jack Antonoff. Nominated for Album of the Year at the 2020 Grammy Awards.
eras.lede: Norman Fucking Rockwell! was released on 30 August 2019. The first full album with Jack Antonoff as a central collaborator, it traded some of the earlier maximalism for soft rock, piano, and a slower, more conversational kind of songwriting.

sections.heading: The record
body: The 14-track album includes “Mariners Apartment Complex”, “Venice Bitch”, “Fuck It I Love You”, “Doin’ Time”, “Cinnamon Girl”, “The Greatest”, and “Hope Is a Dangerous Thing for a Woman Like Me to Have – but I Have It”.

It reached No. 1 in seven countries, including the UK, and No. 3 in the US. It was nominated for Album of the Year at the 62nd Grammy Awards and later entered Rolling Stone’s 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.

sections.heading: Recognition
body: Jack Antonoff was a central producer on the album, released 30 August 2019.
The only NFR photograph in the collection is from the Grammy Museum in October 2019, photographed by Justin Higuchi.

eras.label: Chemtrails / Blue Banisters
eras.title: Chemtrails, Blue Banisters, and the quiet house
eras.summary: Two albums released seven months apart in 2021, alongside a poetry book and a spoken-word record.
eras.lede: In 2020, Del Rey published Violet Bent Backwards over the Grass, a poetry collection with a companion spoken-word album. Chemtrails over the Country Club followed on 19 March 2021; Blue Banisters arrived on 22 October 2021, only seven months later.

sections.heading: Violet
body: The spoken-word album, produced with Jack Antonoff, sets 14 poems against sparse piano and strings. Del Rey reads the poems rather than singing them.
The album appeared in July 2020; the book, published by Simon & Schuster, followed in September. They are listed together because they share the same texts.

sections.heading: Two albums
body: Chemtrails is a folk, country-folk, and Americana record with contributions from Nikki Lane, Weyes Blood, and Zella Day. It debuted at No. 1 in eight countries, including the UK, and No. 2 in the US.
Blue Banisters followed on 22 October 2021, seven months later. It reached No. 8 in the US and No. 1 in Argentina and the Netherlands.

eras.label: Ocean Blvd
eras.title: Ocean Blvd and the tunnel
eras.summary: Sixteen tracks released 24 March 2023, produced with Jack Antonoff, Drew Erickson, and Zach Dawes.
eras.lede: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd was released on 24 March 2023. At 16 tracks and nearly 78 minutes, it is one of Del Rey's densest records, with production from Jack Antonoff, Drew Erickson, Zach Dawes, and others.

sections.heading: The record
body: The album includes “The Grants”, “A&W”, “Candy Necklace”, “Kintsugi”, “Fingertips”, “Paris, Texas”, “Let the Light In”, and “Taco Truck x VB”. It features Jon Batiste, Bleachers, Father John Misty, Tommy Genesis, SYML, and Riopy.
It topped charts in eight countries and reached No. 3 in the US. The album received nominations for Album of the Year and Best Alternative Music Album at the 66th Grammy Awards.

sections.heading: Before and after
body: In 2022, “Snow on the Beach”, a collaboration with Taylor Swift, became Del Rey’s highest-charting entry on the Billboard Hot 100 at the time. In 2023, “Say Yes to Heaven”, recorded a decade earlier, was released officially.
At 77 minutes and 52 seconds, Ocean Blvd is the longest album in the archive. The MITA photograph is a wide black-and-white crowd shot from 2023.

eras.label: Stove
eras.title: Stove and the next chapter
eras.summary: A country project first announced as Lasso in January 2024, renamed twice, and still unreleased on 24 November 2026.
eras.lede: The next chapter has been public for longer than most albums. In January 2024, Del Rey announced a country project called Lasso; by November 2024 it had become The Right Person Will Stay, and in August 2025 she confirmed the title Stove. As of 24 November 2026, the album has not been released.

sections.heading: The singles
body: “Henry, Come On” arrived on 11 April 2025, followed by “Bluebird” on 18 April 2025 and “White Feather Hawk Tail Deer Hunter” on 17 February 2026. At Stagecoach in April 2025, Del Rey performed “Stars Fell on Alabama”, “Quiet in the South”, and “57.5”.
The release was first expected in September 2024, then May 2025, then early 2026. Del Rey said the delay came from adding new material.

sections.heading: The wider frame
body: In 2024, “Tough” with Quavo was released. In 2026, Del Rey was announced as the singer of the theme for the James Bond game 007 First Light, and she appeared on Zach Bryan’s “Lies”.

On 15 July 2026, she said the extra material had become a separate companion album. The artwork suggested the title Spyda; no final title, tracklist, or release date has been confirmed as of 24 November 2026.

albums.title: Kill Kill
albums.label: 5 Points
albums.summary: The first public record: three songs, 13 minutes, and a name that would not last.
narrative: Kill Kill was released on 21 October 2008 under the name Lizzy Grant. Produced by David Kahne, the three-track EP introduces the torch-song register and the trailer-park imagery that would become more legible later.

It is a small record, but it is the archive's starting point. The title track, “Yayo”, and “Gramma (Blue Ribbon Sparkler Trailer Heaven)” already contain the ingredients — the cinematic frame, the worn glamour, the slight remove from the present — that the later albums would amplify.
albums.tracklistNote: Three tracks. The EP was later included in full on the 2010 album Lana Del Ray.

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Out of print; not on major streaming services

albums.title: Lana Del Ray
albums.label: 5 Points
albums.summary: The debut album under the Lizzy Grant name: 13 tracks, a different spelling, and a record that disappeared from sale soon after.
narrative: Lana Del Ray — note the spelling — was released on 4 January 2010 through 5 Points Records. Produced by David Kahne, it collects 13 songs, including new versions of “Kill Kill”, “Gramma”, and “Yayo”.

The album was withdrawn from digital retail after Del Rey signed with a major label; it remains the clearest document of the pre-“Video Games” project. The title is sometimes written Lana Del Ray and sometimes Lana Del Rey; the album cover uses Ray.

albums.title: Born to Die
albums.label: Stranger / Interscope / Polydor
albums.producers: Emile Haynie; Patrik Berger; Justin Parker; Robopop; Rick Nowels; Al Shux
albums.summary: Released 27 January 2012. Twelve tracks on the standard edition; the deluxe edition adds three more.
narrative: Born to Die was released on 27 January 2012 through Interscope and Polydor. The standard edition has 12 tracks; the deluxe edition adds three more.
The album peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard 200. “Video Games”, “Born to Die”, and “Blue Jeans” were released as singles before and around the album.

albums.tracklistNote: Standard edition. The deluxe edition adds “Without You”, “Lolita”, and “Lucky Ones”.

albums.title: Lana Del Rey
albums.label: Stranger
albums.producers: Emile Haynie; Justin Parker; Robopop; Patrik Berger
albums.summary: A four-track introduction released just before the debut album.
narrative: The Lana Del Rey EP was released on 10 January 2012 through Stranger Records. Its four tracks — “Video Games”, “Born to Die”, “Blue Jeans”, and “Off to the Races” — are the clearest early statement of the project's range: one homemade hit, one widescreen ballad, one noir guitar song, and one rap-adjacent curveball.
It is not the same release as the 2010 album Lana Del Ray. The shared name is one of the reasons the early discography needs a careful timeline.

albums.title: Paradise
albums.label: Polydor / Interscope
albums.producers: Rick Nowels; Justin Parker; Rick Rubin; Emile Haynie
albums.summary: Eight tracks of widescreen Americana, plus the iTunes bonus “Burning Desire”.
narrative: Paradise was released on 9 November 2012. Its eight tracks include “Ride”, “American”, “Cola”, “Body Electric”, “Blue Velvet”, “Gods & Monsters”, “Yayo”, and “Bel Air”; the iTunes edition added “Burning Desire”.
It debuted at number ten on the Billboard 200 and was later packaged with Born to Die as The Paradise Edition. The EP is the most direct bridge between the debut album and the Tropico film.

albums.title: Tropico
albums.label: Interscope / Polydor
albums.producers: Rick Nowels; Dan Heath; Emile Haynie; Tim Larcombe
albums.summary: A 27-minute short film built around three Paradise songs.
narrative: Tropico is a 27-minute short film directed by Anthony Mandler, premiered in December 2013. It is structured in three chapters — “Body Electric”, “Gods & Monsters”, and “Bel Air” — and frames the songs as a loose Adam-and-Eve narrative.
The film is listed as a film/soundtrack release because it belongs in the 2012–13 chronology between Paradise and Ultraviolence.

albums.label: Polydor / Interscope
albums.producers: Dan Auerbach; Lana Del Rey; Paul Epworth; Greg Kurstin; Rick Nowels
albums.summary: 11 tracks of live guitar, desert rock, and a harder vocal edge.
narrative: Ultraviolence was released on 13 June 2014. Produced largely with Dan Auerbach, its 11-track standard edition moves from “Cruel World” to “The Other Woman”, with “West Coast”, “Brooklyn Baby”, and “Shades of Cool” at the centre.

It debuted at number one in eleven countries, including the US, and reached the top five in more than twenty territories. The deluxe edition adds “Black Beauty”, “Guns and Roses”, and “Florida Kilos”; the iTunes edition adds “Is This Happiness”, and the Japanese/Target edition adds “Flipside”.

albums.title: Honeymoon
albums.label: Interscope / Polydor
albums.producers: Lana Del Rey; Rick Nowels; Kieron Menzies
albums.summary: A 14-track, 65-minute return to baroque pop, recorded with Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies.
narrative: Honeymoon was released on 18 September 2015. Produced by Del Rey with Rick Nowels and Kieron Menzies, it marked a departure from the guitar-driven Ultraviolence and a return to the baroque pop of Born to Die and Paradise.

The album opens with the title track and moves through “Music to Watch Boys To”, “Terrence Loves You”, “High by the Beach”, “Freak”, and “The Blackest Day”. It peaked at number two on the Billboard 200 and reached the top five in more than twenty countries.
The Endless Summer Tour followed in 2015, with Courtney Love and Grimes on selected dates. In 2016, Del Rey appeared on the Weeknd's “Starboy”.

albums.summary: A 16-track, collaborative record that topped charts in twelve countries and earned a Grammy nomination.
narrative: Lust for Life was released on 21 July 2017. It features the Weeknd, A$AP Rocky, Playboi Carti, Stevie Nicks, and Sean Ono Lennon, and marks a return to the hip-hop-inspired sound of Born to Die alongside the folk and trap-pop textures of the mid-2010s.

The album topped the charts in twelve countries, including the US and the UK, and was nominated for Best Pop Vocal Album at the 60th Grammy Awards. Its 16 tracks include “Love”, “Lust for Life”, “13 Beaches”, “Cherry”, “Summer Bummer”, “Groupie Love”, and “Get Free”.

narrative: Norman Fucking Rockwell! was released on 30 August 2019. Primarily produced by Del Rey and Jack Antonoff, with additional contributions from Zach Dawes, Andrew Watt, and Rick Nowels, it explored soft rock, psych-rock, and piano balladry.

The 14-track album includes “Mariners Apartment Complex”, “Venice Bitch”, “Fuck It I Love You”, “Doin' Time”, “Cinnamon Girl”, “The Greatest”, and “Hope Is a Dangerous Thing for a Woman Like Me to Have – but I Have It”.

It reached number one in seven countries, including the UK, and number three in the US. It was nominated for Album of the Year at the 62nd Grammy Awards and later entered Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.

albums.title: Violet Bent Backwards over the Grass
albums.label: Interscope / Polydor
albums.summary: A poetry collection and a companion spoken-word album: 14 poems, sparse piano, and a different kind of attention.
narrative: Violet Bent Backwards over the Grass began as a poetry collection, published by Simon & Schuster on 29 September 2020. The companion spoken-word album arrived earlier, on 28 July 2020, through Interscope and Polydor, with music by Jack Antonoff.

Its 14 tracks are poems, not songs; the record is best approached as a reading rather than a pop album. The book and the album are related but separate releases, and the archive lists them together because they share a voice and a moment.

narrative: Chemtrails over the Country Club was released on 19 March 2021. Del Rey enlisted Jack Antonoff as her co-producer for most of the album, with Rick Nowels producing one track; the record features Nikki Lane, Weyes Blood, and Zella Day.

It debuted at number one in eight countries, including the UK, and number two in the US. Its 11 tracks include “White Dress”, “Chemtrails over the Country Club”, “Tulsa Jesus Freak”, “Let Me Love You like a Woman”, “Yosemite”, and “For Free”.

albums.label: Interscope / Polydor
albums.producers: Lana Del Rey; Mike Hermosa; Jack Antonoff; Drew Erickson; Zach Dawes; Benji Lysaght
albums.summary: A 16-track, 78-minute album about family, memory, and the stories we build around both.
narrative: Did You Know That There's a Tunnel Under Ocean Blvd was released on 24 March 2023. It features production by Del Rey, Mike Hermosa, Jack Antonoff, Drew Erickson, Zach Dawes, and Benji Lysaght, and collaborations with Jon Batiste, Bleachers, Father John Misty, Tommy Genesis, SYML, and Riopy.

The album includes “The Grants”, “A&W”, “Candy Necklace”, “Kintsugi”, “Fingertips”, “Paris, Texas”, “Let the Light In”, and “Taco Truck x VB”. It topped charts in eight countries and reached number three in the US.
It was nominated for Album of the Year and Best Alternative Music Album at the 66th Grammy Awards. In 2023, “Say Yes to Heaven” — a song recorded a decade earlier — was finally released officially.

albums.producers: Lana Del Rey; Jack Antonoff; Drew Erickson; Luke Laird
albums.summary: The tenth studio album: a country project announced under three titles, delayed, and still pending as of 24 November 2026.
narrative: Stove was first announced in January 2024 as Lasso, renamed The Right Person Will Stay in November 2024, and confirmed as Stove in August 2025. Del Rey described it as a country record and said it would remain close to her earlier work.

Three singles have been released: “Henry, Come On” (11 April 2025), “Bluebird” (18 April 2025), and “White Feather Hawk Tail Deer Hunter” (17 February 2026). At Stagecoach in April 2025, she performed three new songs — “Stars Fell on Alabama”, “Quiet in the South”, and “57.5” — that were expected to appear on the album.

The album did not appear in early 2026. A single, “White Feather Hawk Tail Deer Hunter”, was released on 17 February 2026. On 15 July 2026 Del Rey said the album was close to completion and that the extra material had become a separate companion record.
albums.tracklistNote: No official tracklist has been released. The confirmed singles are “Henry, Come On”, “Bluebird”, and “White Feather Hawk Tail Deer Hunter”.

albums.title: Untitled companion album
albums.label: Interscope / Polydor
albums.summary: Additional material from the Stove sessions, announced as a separate album in July 2026.
narrative: On 15 July 2026, Del Rey announced that the extra material from the Stove sessions had grown into a companion album. The announcement included vinyl artwork for Stove and a second cover featuring a boat named “Spyda”, which suggested a possible title.
No title, tracklist, or release date has been confirmed. The entry records the announcement and the checked-on date, 24 November 2026.

fanNotes.title: How this archive is checked
fanNotes.lede: Two rules govern these pages: dates come from cited sources, and photographs need a named creator and licence.

notes.title: How facts are checked
body: A release date, chart position, or announcement is recorded only when a cited source supports it. Wikipedia is used to find the underlying interview, label notice, or review; the Sources page lists each reference.

Unreleased projects are marked provisional. Stove and the untitled companion album show the date each status was checked: 24 November 2026. Corrections are made in the data file, and every page that uses the fact is rebuilt.

notes.title: How photographs are selected
body: A photograph is used only when its creator, source file page, and licence are visible on Wikimedia Commons. Each image is stored locally and shows its credit on the gallery tile and in the lightbox.
Two periods have no qualifying image in this collection: the early Lizzy Grant years and the Chemtrails / Blue Banisters period. Their tiles are marked as placeholders.

rules: Dates are linked to a named source.
Photographs carry a creator, file page, and licence.
Unreleased material is marked provisional with a checked-on date.
Corrections go into the data file, not the generated HTML.

submit.title: Corrections, takedowns, and licensed photographs
submit.body: Send a correction, a takedown request, or an offer of a licensed photograph through the public issue tracker. Include the page URL and the source you are citing.

about.title: Lizzy to Lana
about.lede: A reference for Lana Del Rey's recorded work: nine eras, sixteen releases, and eighteen credited concert photographs. Last checked 24 November 2026.

sections.heading: What is here
body: Nine era pages, individual album pages, a gallery with 18 licensed photographs, a source list, and a search index. The earliest release is the Kill Kill EP (2008); the newest entry is Stove, still unreleased on 24 November 2026.
Each photograph shows its creator, Commons file page, and licence. Dates and chart positions point to the references on the Sources page.

sections.heading: Status
body: This is an unofficial fan archive. It has no connection to Lana Del Rey, her management, or her labels.
It publishes no full lyrics, fabricated quotations, or speculation about private life.

sections.heading: Editorial checks
body: Dates and chart positions are checked against the cited sources and, where possible, the primary announcement. Stove and its companion album carry the date 24 November 2026.
Unreleased records are marked provisional. Where a title, tracklist, or date has not been confirmed, the entry says so.

sections.heading: Photographs
body: Photographs come from Wikimedia Commons, are stored locally, and are served in AVIF, WebP, and JPEG variants. Each carries its creator, file page, and named Creative Commons licence.
Two periods have no qualifying image in the collection: the early Lizzy Grant years and the Chemtrails / Blue Banisters era. Their tiles are marked as placeholders.

sections.heading: Corrections
body: Use the public issue tracker linked below. Include the page URL and the source for a correction, or the file page and licence for a photograph.
Rights holders can request removal through the same tracker.
